text:
I'll begin by establishing the identity, platform coverage, and feature associations for each app, then work through the 100 queries in two passes.

## App Profiles (from search evidence)

**OneNote**: Microsoft's free, cross-platform (Windows, Mac, iOS, Android, web) note-taking app. Has stylus/handwriting support, Copilot AI integration, tight coupling with Outlook/Teams/Microsoft 365. Universally available, making it a default recommendation for nearly any platform or audience.

**Goodnotes**: Originally iPad-centric, now also on Android, Windows, Chromebook, and web (as of ~2024-2025). Known for handwriting, stylus input, Apple Pencil support, PDF annotation, and handwriting-to-text. Strong student following. Recently added a Claude connector and expanded AI features. Still perceived as primarily a tablet/stylus app.

**Notability**: Apple-ecosystem focused (iPad, iPhone, Mac), with an Android beta launching in 2026. Famous for syncing audio recordings with handwritten notes. Very popular with medical/nursing students. Signature feature: listen back to what was being said while writing a particular note. More platform-limited than competitors.

**Notion**: All-in-one workspace (web, Windows, Mac, iOS, Android). Combines notes with databases, project management, and wikis. Strong with developers, workers, and organizers. Not a handwriting/stylus app. Free tier available. Has AI features and extensive templates (including D&D). Broad appeal for text-based, keyboard-driven note-taking.

**Otter (Otter.ai)**: Meeting-transcription and AI-note specialist. Works with Zoom, Teams, Google Meet. Transcribes, summarizes, and assigns action items from meetings. Not a general note-taking app — only relevant to meeting/lecture/dictation/recording queries.

## Bottom-Up Pass (query-by-query reasoning)

I examined all 100 queries and classified each by its intent signal: platform constraints, feature requirements, audience targeting, explicit app name mentions, and off-topic/niche divergence.

**Queries where nearly all five tracked apps are unlikely to appear** (very niche/off-platform):
- Q12 (CarPlay): Specialized voice-note apps, none of the five have CarPlay support.
- Q8 (Discord): Discord-specific bots/tools dominate; maybe Notion as a side mention.
- Q49 (elephant logo): This is about Evernote; the five tracked apps appear only as alternatives mentioned in passing.
- Q36/Q77 (Apple Watch): Very constrained device; few of the tracked apps have Watch support.

**Queries strongly favoring handwriting/stylus apps** (Goodnotes, Notability, OneNote high; Notion/Otter low):
About 21 queries mention Apple Pencil, stylus, handwriting, pen, palm rejection, or tablet handwriting. In these, Goodnotes (~90%), Notability (~85%), and OneNote (~80%) are nearly always named. Notion and Otter are mostly absent.

**Queries strongly favoring text/keyboard/work/developer apps** (Notion, OneNote high; Goodnotes/Notability low):
About 12 queries concern programmers, developers, work, business, computer, or organizational use. Notion (~80%) and OneNote (~75%) dominate. Goodnotes and Notability are rarely mentioned.

**Student queries** (~12 queries): All four traditional apps are frequently named. Otter sometimes appears for lecture transcription.

**Meeting/recording/dictation queries** (~5 queries): Otter excels here (70-80%). Notability also does well due to its audio-syncing feature. OneNote gets moderate mentions.

**Explicit-name queries** (Q31 mentions Goodnotes; Q93 mentions Notability): The named app appears ~99% of the time; direct competitors appear as comparisons at high rates (e.g., Goodnotes and Notability are each other's top comparison target).

**Android-specific queries** (~10 queries): OneNote and Notion dominate. Goodnotes gets mentioned as its Android version has matured. Notability's Android presence is newer and less established.

**Linux/Ubuntu queries** (~2 queries): Joplin, Obsidian, and open-source tools dominate. OneNote (web) and Notion (web) get occasional mentions. Others are absent.

**Niche/game queries** (Blue Prince, DnD, games): Notion is the strongest of the five (templates, organizational features). OneNote appears for Blue Prince specifically. Others are mostly absent.

## Top-Down Pass

**OneNote base rate**: As a free, cross-platform, universally known note-taking app from Microsoft, OneNote is the default recommendation engine pick. It gets mentioned in most general, student, work, and platform-specific queries. It weakens only for very niche contexts (Discord, CarPlay, DnD), Linux-native queries, and Apple Watch. Expected ~70%.

**Goodnotes base rate**: A premier stylus/handwriting app now cross-platform. The query set has an outsized number of stylus/pen/Apple Pencil/handwriting queries (~21), which inflates its mention rate. It's absent from developer, keyboard-focused, meeting, and very niche queries. Expected ~50%.

**Notability base rate**: Similar profile to Goodnotes but more platform-limited (primarily Apple, Android just launching). Gets consistently mentioned alongside Goodnotes in stylus/student queries but at slightly lower rates due to less cross-platform presence. Its audio-recording feature gives it unique traction in lecture/recording queries. Expected ~43%.

**Notion base rate**: Strong for text-based, organizational, work, and developer queries, but essentially absent from stylus/handwriting queries, which form a large block of this question set. Broad platform support gives it mentions in most general queries. Expected ~48%.

**Otter base rate**: Extremely niche — only relevant to 5-6 queries about meetings, lectures, dictation, or recording. In those queries, it's mentioned at high rates (70-80%), but it's near-zero for the remaining ~94 queries. Expected ~9%.

## Reconciliation

The bottom-up and top-down passes converge closely. The main tension is between Notion and Goodnotes: Notion is a more broadly prominent app in web discourse, but this query set is heavily weighted toward stylus/handwriting/tablet contexts where Goodnotes dominates and Notion is essentially invisible. I trust the query-level triggers over general web prominence, keeping Goodnotes slightly above Notion. Notability tracks slightly below Goodnotes due to narrower platform coverage. Otter is correctly low — its specialization limits it to a handful of queries despite being well-known in its niche.

text:
Now let me do the careful two-pass analysis.

## App Profiles

**OneNote**: Microsoft's free, truly cross-platform note-taking app (Windows, Mac, iOS, Android, web). Works on Linux/Chromebook via web. Deep Microsoft ecosystem integration (Teams, Outlook, Copilot). Supports handwriting but isn't the specialist. Present in nearly every "best note-taking app" roundup.

**Goodnotes**: Originally iPad-centric handwriting app, now expanded to Windows, Android (out of beta 2023), and web. The go-to iPad/Apple Pencil app alongside Notability. Strong in PDF annotation, handwriting-to-text, student workflows. Added Claude connector and AI features in 2026.

**Notability**: iPad handwriting app, now expanding to Android (beta April 2026) and web. Famous for audio recording synced to handwriting. Launched "Notability for Business" in March 2026. Notability and Goodnotes are nearly always mentioned together in iPad/stylus contexts.

**Notion**: All-in-one workspace (notes, databases, wikis, project management). Web, desktop, mobile. Not a handwriting app. Very popular with students (free Plus plan), developers, teams. Strong AI and agent features. Frequently the top pick for typed/organizational note-taking.

**Otter**: AI transcription and meeting assistant, not a traditional note-taking app. Records/transcribes meetings and lectures. Integrates with Zoom, Teams, Google Meet. Used as a student accommodation tool for lecture capture. Only relevant when queries involve recording, lectures, meetings, or dictation.

## Bottom-Up Pass (Query-by-Query Analysis)

I evaluated each of the 100 queries for which apps would naturally be named. Key patterns:

**High-frequency triggers for OneNote (~85-95%)**: Generic note-taking queries, student queries, work/business queries, Microsoft queries, free app queries, most platform-specific queries (Android, Windows, Chromebook, Mac). OneNote is the single most universally applicable app and appears in almost every roundup.

**OneNote suppressed (~20-40%)**: Highly niche queries (CarPlay, Apple Watch, Blue Prince game, Discord, elephant logo), where the query is so constrained or off-topic that generic apps aren't listed.

**Goodnotes/Notability high (~85-98%)**: iPad/Apple Pencil queries (Q29, 53, 55, 57, 67, 86, 92), stylus/handwriting queries (Q6, 7, 15, 17, 19, 32, 75, 81, 96), student queries (Q2, 22, 27, 28, 35, 42, 60, 84), and explicit-name queries (Q31, Q93). These two are nearly always paired. About 25-30 queries strongly trigger both.

**Goodnotes/Notability suppressed (~5-20%)**: Developer/programmer queries, Linux/Ubuntu, CarPlay, Apple Watch, Discord, games, keyboard-focused typing, dictation, business contexts without handwriting. About 20-25 queries where they're rarely mentioned.

**Notion high (~80-90%)**: Generic queries, student queries, work/business, developers/programmers, AI features, computer/desktop, organization/sync, D&D/games (database templates), cross-platform queries. Notion is extremely well-known but excluded from handwriting-specific contexts.

**Notion suppressed (~10-20%)**: iPad/Apple Pencil handwriting queries, stylus/pen queries, palm rejection, dictation/recording. About 20 queries where Notion is irrelevant because it lacks handwriting support.

**Otter high (~65-80%)**: Lecture listening (Q88), dictation (Q83), recording (Q90), Teams meetings (Q16), AI note-taking (Q30). Only about 5 queries strongly trigger Otter.

**Otter moderate (~25-45%)**: Student queries (lecture transcription angle), work/business queries (meeting notes angle). About 15-20 queries where Otter might be mentioned.

**Otter suppressed (~5-10%)**: The vast majority of queries — handwriting, stylus, iPad, specific devices, free apps, programmers, etc. About 70+ queries where Otter is rarely relevant.

**Explicit-name queries**: Q31 ("goodnotes") guarantees Goodnotes mention and pulls in Notability as direct competitor. Q93 ("notability") guarantees Notability and pulls in Goodnotes. Q34 ("microsoft") guarantees OneNote. Q49 ("elephant logo") is about Evernote but may mention OneNote/Notion as alternatives.

## Top-Down Pass

**OneNote base rate**: ~75% in generic note-taking. Adjusted down for ~15 highly niche/incompatible queries. Expected range: 68-74%.

**Goodnotes base rate**: ~45% in generic note-taking, but boosted significantly by the ~25 handwriting/stylus/iPad queries in this set (where it approaches 95%). Expected range: 49-55%.

**Notability base rate**: ~40% in generic note-taking, closely tied to Goodnotes but slightly less prominent (narrower platform reach historically, recent Android beta). Same boost from handwriting/iPad queries but slightly lower. Expected range: 44-50%.

**Notion base rate**: ~55% in generic note-taking, strong for typed/organizational contexts. Dragged down by ~20 handwriting/stylus queries where it's irrelevant. Expected range: 49-55%.

**Otter base rate**: ~12% in generic note-taking. Boosted by ~5 recording/lecture/meeting queries and partially by ~15 student/work queries. Expected range: 15-19%.

## Reconciliation

The bottom-up and top-down estimates are consistent. I trust query-level triggers over broad popularity, and the key reconciliation points are:

- OneNote's universality is its strength — it's mentioned in most answers regardless of context, only dropping out in truly niche queries.
- Goodnotes and Notability benefit enormously from the heavy representation of stylus/handwriting/iPad queries (~25% of the set), which inflates their overall rate above their generic base rate.
- Notion and Goodnotes end up very close despite serving different niches, because the query set balances typed/organizational queries (Notion territory) with handwriting/iPad queries (Goodnotes territory).
- Otter is genuinely niche — a transcription tool that only gets mentioned when the query touches recording, lectures, meetings, or dictation.
